svg.text: Half-size breadboard seen from above. Rows 1-30 run down, columns a-j across. The ESP32's USB-C is at row 1, the power module at row 30.
Only the right side is wired: the ESP32's 5V, GND, D13, D14 and D27 pins are all in column i, so every wire starts in column j.
power it from the 9V battery clip or its USB-A socket
any hole on the blue rail
Plug it into the rails at the row 30 end
(the USB-C is in the way at row 1),
+ on the red rail, − on the blue rail.
Power it from the 9V battery or USB-A,
Turn the power module off first,
then plug the USB-C cable in.
Unplug it and turn the module back on
The pin names are printed on the ESP32
next to each pin. Before powering on,
check i1 is 5V, i6 is GND,
i5 is D13, i8 D14 and i9 D27.
Index tip: next page (hold to keep going)
